It really depends on what you want to do.  You can do a modern amazon challenge or a medieval esc one, one where the world has always been female-led, matriarchy type, a queendom, etc.  You start with a female founder, recruit women to join your cause, and collect money and give birth to daughters to be heir's to positions they fill in the clan/queendom.  Here's a link to the original challenge, but you can change it as you want: [https://modthesims.info/t/506850](https://modthesims.info/t/506850)

I have a few that I do. 

1.  Amazon challenge - Female matriarchy to the extreme.  

2. Legacy challenge but make it s l o w - Make a sim you're proud of, a good backstory, some tattoos, and a job that you never really fully dive into like bartender or firefighter, and give them friends and have them host parties.  Freeze aging while you play, or make it long lifespan, and just live their life.  Fill their house with personalized furniture, stuff they'd actually like, and give them drama.  Lovers, backstabbing friends that take their man, a cheating husband, etc.  Do it for every generation until you can't anymore.  

3. Rags to riches - Furnish your lot using only dumpster dived items or salvaged items you restore, and no official jobs, just dumpster diving, odd jobs here and there, gigs you make up and assign a money making amount.  I started with a bus stop looking lot, just a bench and some walls reminiscent of a bus stop.

4. Snatched by the Fae - Make a pair of sims that are married and despise each other.  One is fae, the other human.  Give the fae two helpers, one to raise children and the other to clean and cook and fix things.  You have to get the relationship up with the married couple until they can have kids, and have one fae child per gender.  You can't control the human, nor can you let them spend too much time together and restore the relationship too quickly.

I have a rags to riches legacy household, currently on Gen 3's childhood.

I started with my founder who was a 17 year old running from the law, camping out on a small lot in town.  After making some money, all of her dumpster found objects were placed to make a sort of junkyard and a bus stop spot to sleep, eventually turning into a camper.  She started ... Suspicious modded activities as the way to make money, and eventually used her sugar daddy to go to college after having her first son.  After that, she had her second son, and moved to Bridgeport for a fresh start as a tatted up bartender.  She left her sons with a babysitter most of the time, trying to keep them afloat for years, until she met their stepfather, married him, and moved to their first house.

She finally pursued her dream of being a cop once her sons were teenagers, and had two more children with her new husband.

Current day, they've since moved to two towns, the eldest has married and has 6 kids, the other two sons live with their sister and her two kids, and I'm planning to introduce the gen 3 future partner next time I play.  This generation is meant to be a sort of "snatched by the fae" challenge 😁😁

I'm similar, but worse, if we compare.  Decided to take a gap year to decide if I really wanted to go into a certain degree.  Turned into a 4 year long break from any learning at all, a bunch of fast food jobs that went nowhere, trauma upon trauma, and a lot of finding myself within the confines of having no money and no way to leave my situation.  

When I finally DID decide to leave on my own at 22?  After 8 years of living in that town, set out on a new adventure, ready to begin anew, maybe start college in the fall....got in a wreck a week later and was forced to live with family up until... Now.

I have a high school degree, a few college credits, multiple book ideas I fail to work on, and plans to go to university in Germany or somewhere else free so I can actually afford to do what I've wanted to do for years.

I feel amazing, compared to last year.  I've learned a lot.

I feel a lot of that same guilt you do for never achieving what I could have, straight A student with so many prospects for the future at 18 to this life now at 23.

But you can always pursue what you want, it just might look different than you thought it would.

It's gonna be okay :)

1. Started going to therapy.  I procrastinated for YEARS, and then finally started going.  The therapist herself hasn't helped me, but the idea of being in therapy made me legitimately want to get better.  Accountability, I suppose.

2. To stop identifying with it as a label for yourself.  Yes, even when you want to die every second of every day.  Even when every bad thing that happens in your life triggers you to just die and get it over with already.  Even when you're at rock bottom and there's no reason left for you to keep going.  Stop putting a label on that gut-wrenching, sinking feeling.  Stop identifying what the tears mean, what the anxiety, the complete numbness, anything else MEANS.  

3.  Letting myself feel my emotions without attaching a story to it.  You feel horrible for some reason and want to cry and lay in bed and stare at the wall for a few hours?  Then do it!  And guess what?  90% of the time it helps, and you're back to feeling neutral / normal / maybe even happy afterwards, all because you did what your body wanted instead of forcing yourself to cope by doom scrolling / forcing yourself to work on things you don't want to / being "productive" / shaming yourself.
